explanation: NearBlocks documents neither count, but the numbers show what each one is. v1 matches Nansen's published distinct signers, and v3 stays within 2% of v1 plus meta_accounts, so it also counts users whose transactions a relayer signs. The gap is therefore the size of relayed activity: about 2x since April 2026, but 9x to 18x in monthly averages before 2026-04-02, when a Kai-Ching batch of about 2,000,000 accounts a day stopped and a Sweat key migration ended. Both counts are kept here, and neither is called daily active users.

metric: Mean daily active contracts over 30 days
Contracts active per day, mean over the days both sources hold
source_a: BigQuery, distinct accounts that received a function call
explanation: These are not one count. BigQuery's figure is the distinct accounts that received a function call that day, about 1,100 a day since April 2026. NearBlocks does not document what its active contracts figure holds; over the same days it averages about 84,000, some 80 times larger, and it rises and falls with the accounts a relayer signed for (correlation 0.9), not with the contracts called (correlation -0.25). So it follows relayed accounts, not contracts. Nothing on the site or in the thesis reads it.

metric: NEAR burned on the days before issuance began
source_b: Fall in total supply on the same days
explanation: Expected: the burn figure is a lower bound, and this is the one place it can be measured. Before issuance began on 2020-10-20 nothing was minted, so every fall in total supply was gas burned. Over those 79 days supply fell by 124.4 NEAR against gas fees of 146.8 NEAR, which is 84.8% of gas, while the burn figure takes 70%. The contracts' share was 30% of the gas burnt executing function calls, not of all gas, so the real burn was always more than 70% of the fee and never more than all of it. The lower bound held on every one of the 79 days, and a test keeps it so. The 84.8% belongs to 2020's mix of transactions, so it is not applied to later years; treat the burn figure before 2026-11-04 as a floor. From that day protocol version 87 burns all gas and the figure is exact.
